cards.text: Welcome to Mags's station, friend, where Moses, Israel's leader, speaks to all Israel in the wilderness east of the Jordan. Before he starts, a quick travel note. From Horeb to Kadesh-barnea is an eleven-day journey.

cards.question: Hold that eleven days in your head. Moses gives this speech to the Israelites in the ___ year.

cards.text: Eleven days, forty years, and I'm just gonna set those two side by side and back away SLOWLY. By now, Moses has defeated Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan.

cards.question: On the east side of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses begins to ___ this law.

cards.text: Moses starts his sermon way back at Horeb. That's where the LORD our God spoke to them about the mountain they'd been staying at.

cards.question: At Horeb, what does the LORD tell the people about that mountain?

answers.text: You have stayed at this mountain long enough
Build an altar to Me on this mountain
Stay at this mountain for one more year

cards.text: If anybody had told me "long enough" back in the junk drawer, friend, I'd have been GONE before that drawer finished opening. God tells them to go on to the hill country of the Amorites and all the lands around it, as far as Lebanon and the great River Euphrates.

cards.question: God says, "See, I have placed the land before you." Which fathers did the LORD swear He would give this land to?

cards.text: Then Moses reminds them what he said back then: "I cannot carry the burden for you alone." Picture one man running a group chat with the whole nation in it.

cards.question: Why can't Moses carry the people alone anymore? What has the LORD done to them?

answers.text: Made them as numerous as the stars
Scattered them across the whole desert
Split them into two separate camps

cards.text: The man is BURIED in people, and he still says, "May the LORD, the God of your fathers, increase you a thousand times over and bless you as He has promised."

cards.question: Moses can't bear all their troubles, burdens and disputes by himself. So what does he tell the people to do?

answers.text: Choose wise men from each tribe
Cast lots for one new leader
Settle every dispute on their own

cards.question: True or false: Moses picks the new leaders all by himself, without the tribes choosing anyone.

cards.text: And the people answer, "What you propose to do is good." A whole nation agreeing on one plan, and friend, that group chat could NEVER.

cards.question: Moses takes the wise and respected leaders of the tribes and appoints them. How does he set them up?

answers.text: In ranks from thousands down to tens
One leader over each single family
Twelve leaders all equal in rank

cards.text: Then Moses gives the judges their orders. Hear the disputes between their brothers and judge fairly.

cards.question: True or false: the judges are to judge fairly between fellow Israelites, but not when a foreign resident is involved.
Moses tells the judges to show no partiality and hear small and great alike. Don't be intimidated by anyone, he says, because judgment belongs to ___.
True or false: when a case is too difficult for the judges, Moses tells them to bring it to him.

cards.text: Moses wraps this part up: at that time, he commanded them all the things they were to do. But Moses is only warming up, friend, and this sermon is far from done.

findings.problem: The choice card's question is the only place Deuteronomy 1:12 is told (Moses can't bear their troubles, burdens and disputes by himself). That setup isn't on any story card. Card 11 cites only 1:11, and card 12 cites only 1:13, so 1:12 is never cited on any card. Move the 1:12 beat onto card 11 (citing Deuteronomy 1:11-12) or onto a new story card. The question can then restate it as context.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: Card 13 (true or false: Moses picks the leaders by himself, without the tribes choosing) tests the same fact card 12 just asked, that the tribes choose the men (Deuteronomy 1:13). It flips the wording but adds nothing new. The docs allow 'an easy follow-up,' but their example (the lesser light rules the night) tests a new fact. Other details in 1:13-15 go untested, such as the qualities Moses asks for (wise, understanding, respected) or that Moses is the one who appoints them.
findings.question: Can a follow-up choice card re-test the exact fact the card before it just asked, or must an easy follow-up test a new fact?
